Hi Catherine — quick technical summary addressing your numbered items. I can expand on any section in the walkthrough.

1) PHI persistence:
- By default, Redwood Hosted does not persist request/response payloads containing PHI beyond short-term operational buffers used for streaming and KV cache. Those buffers are in-memory; we truncate/evict on session end.
- Customers can opt into persistent logs for debugging; that requires explicit configuration and is off by default.

2) Logical segmentation / multi-tenancy:
- Tenant isolation is enforced at three layers: (a) tenant-scoped model routing (requests tagged with tenant id), (b) per-tenant KV cache namespaces to prevent cross-tenant cache hits, and (c) RBAC & ACL checks at the serving gateway.
- All inter-process communication uses mTLS with mutual certs and policy-based authorization between services.

3) Retention windows:
- Default request/response log retention: 0 days (ephemeral) for production PHI-in-scope flows unless customer enables.
- Audit logs (access events/metadata) are stored 90 days by default; customers can request custom retention (including export & purge workflows).

4) Key management:
- Hosted: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS). Keys are used for encrypting stored artifacts and model cache checkpoints.
- For BYOK, customer keys are used to wrap tenant-specific data encryption keys; Redwood rotates tenant keys every 30 days (by default) but will honor customer rotation policies if provided.

5) Evidence and BAA: Monica will follow up with SOC 2 Type II summary and our BAA template. Note: our SOC 2 report covers the Hosted platform; Dedicated/Private deployments have separate evidence streams.

Operational controls we’ll cover in the walkthrough: dataflow diagrams for inference, KV cache eviction policy, how we implement redaction and prompt filtering, and options for model caching disablement for PHI-sensitive routes.

On scheduling — we can do May 26 at 10:00am PT. Confirm and I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda (15m architecture, 20m demo, 10m Q&A).
